DPZ.thesis_one_line: World's largest pizza franchisor, collecting royalties on franchisee sales; cheap-looking multiple but growth just decelerated and guidance was already cut once this year.
kill_criteria: U.S. same-store sales negative for two consecutive quarters.
FY operating-income-growth guidance cut again below the current mid-to-high-single-digit range.
Debt + capital-lease obligations / EBITDA-proxy rises above 6.0x (from ~4.8x currently).
International same-store sales (ex-FX) negative for two consecutive quarters.
Quarterly buyback pace cut by more than half from the trailing-4-quarter average (signal of FCF/leverage stress in the securitization structure).
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 operating-income-growth guidance was CUT at the Q1 2026 release (from ~8% to mid-to-high-single-digit) on weaker U.S./international same-store sales guidance, then only held flat (not raised) at Q2 2026 -- not a 'guidance raised' story.
Q2 2026 U.S. same-store sales were +0.1%, the weakest in over a year and below the +0.62% consensus; international SSS ex-FX was -0.1% vs +0.5% expected.

Stockholders' equity is deeply negative (-$3.98bn at 2026-06-14) and debt+capital leases were $4.82bn at FY2025-end -- a whole-business-securitization, buyback-funded structure that is by design but leaves less balance-sheet slack than the headline P/E suggests.

An ongoing securities class action (filed 2024, status ONGOING as of 2025-06-11) alleges Domino's failed to disclose execution problems at its largest master franchisee (DPE) and was unlikely to meet its own long-term global net-store-growth guidance.
U.S. net-store-growth target was trimmed to ~175 stores from '175-plus' at the Q2 2026 release.
data_conflicts: Triage's reason ('14.3x NTM P/E for high-teens EPS growth... looks like value') did not check the prior guidance range; this dossier finds guidance was cut once (Q1'26) and only held flat since (Q2'26), and recent same-store-sales trends (U.S. +0.1% in Q2'26) are weaker than the triage framing implies.

b1 momentum percentile (1st) and book/price percentile (1st, driven by negative equity from buybacks) are not informative on their own for this capital structure; flagged so they are not misread as distress signals.
DPZ.confidence_in_thesis: medium (guidance cut and soft U.S. comps are recent and real, but FCF/buyback execution and international World Cup tailwind are also verified from primary sources; no V1 row exists to cross-check the valuation view)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DPZ has no V1 row (outside the top-70 quant-ranked universe covered by the systematic valuation model), so there is nothing to reconcile; v1_verdict is null per the standing rule for names without systematic coverage.

EME.thesis_one_line: Largest U.S. electrical/mechanical contractor riding the AI data-center construction boom, with three straight guidance raises and a net-cash balance sheet -- but the growth driver is concentrated and cyclical.
kill_criteria: RPO/backlog growth turns negative YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +32.9% YoY as of 2026-03-31).
Full-year revenue or EPS guidance is cut, breaking the current three-release raise streak.
Consolidated operating margin falls below 8.5% for two consecutive quarters (vs 8.7-12.7% range over the last 8 quarters).
Net cash position flips to net debt exceeding 1.0x EBITDA.
Cumulative operating cash flow over any trailing 4 quarters falls below 50% of cumulative EBITDA over the same period.
key_adverse_facts: Growth is concentrated in AI/data-center capex (Network & Communications segment); management itself flags labor availability, wage inflation and cyclical industrial/oil-and-gas exposure as ongoing risks even while raising guidance.

Operating cash flow fell YoY in FY2025 ($1,302mm vs $1,408mm in FY2024) despite EPS growth, and Q1 2026 OCF was essentially zero ($0.558mm) before rebounding -- consistent with working-capital consumption as the backlog ramps; this was not fully decomposed against contract-asset/unbilled-revenue growth (data limitation).
Analyst coverage is thin (7 analysts per the live snapshot), increasing model/estimate risk on both the bull and bear case.

The stock has re-rated from a historical mid-teens P/E (2019-2023) to 20-24x since the data-center buildout began, so much of the good news (record backlog, guidance raises) already appears reflected in the price.
data_conflicts: Triage flagged EME as 'underappreciated' at 21.3x NTM P/E vs FIX/PWR at 29-34x; the current live snapshot shows a 20.7x forward P/E, meaning the valuation gap versus that peer set has already narrowed materially since the 2026-08-18 triage snapshot -- the 'underappreciated' framing is weaker today than when triage was run.
EME.confidence_in_thesis: medium (guidance/backlog trend is unambiguous and well-documented across three consecutive releases, but durability of the data-center capex cycle beyond 2-3 years, and the cash-conversion working-capital swing, are genuine open questions; no V1 row exists to cross-check valuation)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: EME has no V1 row (outside the top-70 quant-ranked universe covered by the systematic valuation model), so there is nothing to reconcile; v1_verdict is null per the standing rule for names without systematic coverage.

FANG.thesis_one_line: Largest low-cost Permian oil producer post-Endeavor merger, actively paying down debt -- but today's 'cheap' multiple is inflated by a geopolitically-driven oil-price spike, not a structural repricing.
kill_criteria: WTI averages below $50/bbl for two consecutive quarters.
A third consecutive-year ceiling-test impairment of oil and gas properties in any of the next four quarters.
Full-year oil production guidance is cut from the current >522 MBO/d target.
The base dividend (currently $4.40/share annualized) is cut.
key_adverse_facts: GAAP results carried two large non-cash ceiling-test impairments of oil and gas properties confirmed against the primary XBRL tag: $3,652mm in FY2025 (essentially all in Q4 2025) and a further $1,400mm in Q1 2026, driving a derived Q4 2025 net loss (~$1.46bn) and a near-breakeven Q1 2026 (net income $25mm on $4.24bn revenue).

WTI closed ~$93/bbl on 2026-09-25, up over 50% from roughly a year earlier, attributed in market commentary to acute Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz supply-disruption risk with negotiations reportedly underway to de-escalate -- current profitability and the 'cheap' forward P/E (9.95x) both depend on this holding, not on a $65-70/bbl mid-cycle deck.

Independent (non-primary-sourced) commentary flags insider selling and post-merger integration risk; this was not independently verified against Form 4 filings in this pass (data limitation, disclosed).

Trailing P/E (35.6x) is distorted upward by the impairments and forward P/E (9.95x) is distorted downward by the current price spike -- neither is usable unadjusted, per the sector playbook's explicit warning that low P/E in this sector often marks the top of the cycle.
data_conflicts: Triage called the low trailing/high-vs-NTM P/E gap 'depressed-base noise' and did not identify the two ceiling-test impairments or the oil-price-spike context behind the low forward multiple; this dossier finds both are real, verifiable, and change the valuation read from 'cheap' to 'fair'.

b1 value percentile (23rd) is actually LOW, in some tension with triage's framing of the name via a 9.6% normalized FCF yield as pricing 'near-zero growth' (i.e., cheap); the low b1 value percentile likely reflects book/price and earnings-yield inputs distorted by the same impairments and price-spike effects flagged above.
FANG.confidence_in_thesis: medium (balance-sheet deleveraging and low breakeven cost are well-documented and durable; the current-quarter profitability level is explicitly not durable at spot oil prices, which is the core uncertainty; no V1 row exists to cross-check valuation)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: FANG has no V1 row (outside the top-70 quant-ranked universe covered by the systematic valuation model), so there is nothing to reconcile; v1_verdict is null per the standing rule for names without systematic coverage.
